solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Racehorse, however unkempt, initially black, then scarlet

parts.note: tho is an informal shortening of though, meaning however
unkempt hair or grounds look rough

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word black

parts.note: scarlet is a bright shade of red

explanation.surface: A scruffy-looking racehorse is described as black at first and then scarlet, perhaps by its silks.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree horse of the breed used in flat and jump racing is the classic racehorse.

clue.text: The rain ruined covering for thatch?

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of the words the rain are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Bad weather has spoilt a thatched roof's protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatch' is slang for a head of hair, hence the question mark; the surface suggests a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn to hold hair in place covers one's thatch, a jokey word for hair.

clue.text: Store tracks film from the 1990s

parts.note: a reservoir is a store or reserve, especially of water
to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: A shop's music tracks are said to come from a 1990s film soundtrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino's debut heist movie was released in 1992, so it is a film of that decade.

clue.text: Loud outcry raised, on river with paddle

parts.note: something raised is up
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps
an oar is a paddle for rowing

explanation.surface: A noisy protest goes up on the river among people with paddles.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or clamour of public protest is a loud outcry.

clue.text: Dance in euphoric state with cast

parts.note: someone euphoric is high
a land is a country or state
to cast something is to fling it

explanation.surface: Someone dances in a blissful mood alongside the rest of a show's cast.
explanation.definitionFit: This energetic solo Scottish folk dance is performed at gatherings and competitions.

clue.text: Memorial of antiquity priest kept in church

indicators.note: kept in means the priest's name is held inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: RC stands for the Roman Catholic church
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: An ancient memorial to a priest is preserved inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An object surviving from the distant past, kept as a remembrance, is a survival of antiquity.

clue.text: One accurately shoots lifeless London landmark

parts.note: something lifeless is dead
the London Eye is the big observation wheel on the Thames

explanation.surface: A marksman takes aim at a dull London tourist attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Eye is a giant Ferris wheel on London's South Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack shot who rarely misses is called by this nickname.

clue.text: Type of guitar graduate strums peripherally

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: peripherally takes only the edge letters of the word strums

explanation.surface: A new graduate idly strums a guitar of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-string, low-pitched instrument in a band is one kind of guitar.

clue.text: Di leaves daily records for person born in early April

indicators.note: leaves means the name Di departs, taken out of the records word

parts.note: diaries are daily records
taken as written

explanation.surface: Diana abandons her journals for someone with an April birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born between late March and about 19 April has the Ram as their star sign.

clue.text: Artilleryman keeping agile, having moved royal insignia

indicators.note: keeping means the artilleryman's letters hold the rearranged word inside

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for an artilleryman

indicators.note: having moved means the letters of agile have been shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A nimble gunner has relocated the crown jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agile' reads as the gunner's quality, but 'having moved' scrambles it to EGALI; RA is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: The emblems and ornaments of royalty, such as crown and sceptre, are its regalia.

clue.text: Vocalised melody, knocked back alcoholic cocktail

parts.note: to vocalise a tune is to sing it, so vocalised is sang

indicators.note: knocked back means the word for melody is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: an air is a melody

explanation.surface: Someone sang a tune and downed a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns AIR into RIA; the drinking sense of the phrase is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and spirits is a classic mixed alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Riches entice grabbing Conservative

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for entice seizes the abbreviation and holds it inside

parts.note: to lure is to entice

explanation.surface: Wealth tempts someone into snatching a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Money, particularly when gained dishonourably, is filthy wealth or riches.

clue.text: Opening section of play maybe concerning battle

parts.note: Act I is the first section of a stage play
on means concerning or about

explanation.surface: The first part of a drama might be about a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers seeing combat are said to be in this, a synonym of fighting.

clue.text: Maybe worker to benefit taking in constant medication for stomach?

parts.note: an ant is one example of a worker insect

indicators.note: taking in means the word for benefit encloses the constant's symbol

parts.note: aid is help or benefit
C is the symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics

explanation.surface: A worker might get some benefit from stomach medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts C inside AID, making ACID.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet that neutralises excess stomach acid relieves indigestion, a remedy for the gut.

clue.text: Single digger regularly nervous

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word digger, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A lone excavator worker is often anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being tense and jumpy describes someone nervous.

clue.text: European starts to look around Windsor, an ancient part of England

parts.note: a Dane, from Denmark, is a European

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A Danish visitor begins to explore Windsor, an old part of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of medieval England ruled under Viking law was named for its Danish settlers.

clue.text: Sid reflected inside a long time — did he have a light-bulb moment?

definitions.text: did he have a light-bulb moment?

indicators.note: inside means the turned name goes within the long-time word

parts.note: an eon is a very long time

indicators.note: reflected means the name Sid is mirrored, read backwards

explanation.surface: Sid has reflected for ages, wondering whether he had a bright idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' looks like Sid thinking, but it turns the name round to DIS; the question mark marks the definition as a playful hint at the inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison developed a practical incandescent lamp, so a bulb moment fits the American inventor literally.

clue.text: Tall building initially tempts one in debt

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word tempts

parts.note: an ower is someone who owes, one in debt

explanation.surface: A skyscraper at first lures someone who owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: A high structure such as a skyscraper or castle keep is a tall building.

clue.text: Meander is a feature of some rivers around east

indicators.note: around means the river feature's letters wrap themselves about the compass point

parts.note: waves appear on some rivers, such as a tidal bore
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A meander, the winding bend of a river, is described around the east.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander or zigzag, moving in and out like a thread.

clue.text: American officer, rejected by UN court, no longer working

indicators.note: rejected means the officer's word is turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent, an FBI officer

explanation.surface: A US official is turned away by a United Nations tribunal and is now out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extinct or obsolete, no longer functioning, is defunct in the sense of dead.

clue.text: Biting pastry dish

definitions.meaning: a biting remark is sharp or sour
an open pie with a pastry base and fruit filling

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sharp-tasting or caustic and an open pie with a pastry base.

clue.text: Mostly damp after tea — this might clean the car

indicators.note: after means the reduced damp word comes after the tea word

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: mostly means the word for damp loses its last letter

parts.note: damp means moist

explanation.surface: After a cuppa, something slightly wet might be used to wash the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft leather cloth from goatskin is used for polishing car paintwork and windows.

clue.text: Layabout seen in bridle road

indicators.note: seen in means the letters lie in plain view within the words bridle road

explanation.surface: A loafer is spotted on a bridleway.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who avoids work is a layabout or loafer.

clue.text: Perhaps HP, finally identifying private robe

parts.note: HP Sauce is a British brown sauce, an example of a dressing

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word identifying

parts.note: one's own is private, personal

explanation.surface: A sauce bottle finally identifies a private's robe.
explanation.walkthrough: HP Sauce is a popular British brown table sauce; 'Perhaps' says it is one example of a dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose robe worn over nightclothes at home is a bathrobe-type garment.
